question: Explain the definite integral of x squared from 0 to 1 using an area picture and compute it.

acts.beat: Set up the graph and identify the bounded area.
Approximate the area with increasingly thin rectangles.
Evaluate the exact area using an antiderivative.

panels.title: The region
panels.question: What area represents the integral?
panels.new_idea: Graph y=x² and focus on the region between x=0 and x=1 above the x-axis.
panels.caption: The integral is the area under y=x² from zero to one.

panels.title: Rectangular estimate
panels.question: How can the curved area be approximated?
panels.new_idea: Show rectangles under the curve whose widths become progressively narrower.
panels.caption: Thin rectangles approximate the curved region more closely.

panels.title: Exact computation
panels.question: What is the exact area?
panels.new_idea: Use the antiderivative x³/3 and evaluate it at the endpoints: 1³/3−0³/3=1/3.
panels.caption: The antiderivative gives one-third minus zero, or one-third.

panels.title: Meaning of the result
panels.question: What does one-third represent?
panels.new_idea: Connect the calculation back to the shaded region under the parabola.
panels.caption: Thus the exact shaded area under x² on [0,1] is one-third.

takeaway: The definite integral ∫₀¹ x² dx equals [x³/3]₀¹ = 1/3; the picture motivates the area, while the antiderivative computes it exactly.
